newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, Nikkei pokes above 18,500.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, Nikkei pokes above 18,500.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended sharply higher on Monday with the Nikkei benchmark average closing above 18,500 for the first time in about a month, buoyed by buying of chemical and steel stocks as well as continued short-covering in financial sector issues, brokers said.

The 225-share Nikkei average finished 199.52 points or 1.09 percent higher at 18,551.66, after moving in positive territory for the entire session and hitting an intraday high of 18,560.66. The last time the benchmark closed above 18,500 was on March 21, when it ended at 18,633.16.
June Nikkei futures added 180 points to end at 18,580.

"Index-linked buying, possibly by public funds, appeared once again today to provide the Nikkei average with support," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "Market sentiment has improved considerably."
Winners swamped losers 942 issues to 206, while 95 issues were unchanged. Turnover totalled 451 million shares, compared with 565 million on Friday.

Brokers said share buying that emerged late last week continued into this week, with raw material issues such as chemicals, steels and textiles well-bid. Buy-backs were also noted in the banking and construction sectors.
"Blue-chips are taking a breather now and will probably stay dormant unless currencies start to fluctuate or earnings are announced," Hisao Suzuki, Yamaichi Securities deputy general manager, said.
"Investors are instead choosing to buy lower-priced shares backed by firm earnings," Suzuki added.
Nippon Steel Corp rose seven yen to 365, with trade totalling 10.73 million shares, making it the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
It was followed by Showa Denko KK with 7.25 million shares. The chemicals firm climbed 12 yen to 306, a new high for the calendar year.
Mitsubishi Chemical Corp also hit a new high for the year, adding 13 yen to 423. It was the fourth-most heavily traded issue with 5.93 million shares changing hands.
Brokers said the continued buy-backs of banks, construction firms and brokerages were easing fears of a share price slide led by bad-loan strapped sectors, as seen earlier in the year.

"It looks like pension funds have finally started shopping for stocks for the new fiscal year," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "As long as they are buying, investors are afraid of being caught with short positions and they are hestiating to sell."
Fuji Bank Ltd added 20 yen to 1,500. Contractor Obayashi Corp jumped 20 yen to 640. Yamaichi Securities recovered to end a yen higher at 355.

The brokerage's shares fell to a low of 345 yen due to a newspaper report that Yamaichi, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, reimbursed Hanwa Co Ltd for investment losses in 1992. Yamaichi later denied the report and said it would file libel suits against a Japanese newspaper and a business magazine.
Air transport, sea transport, construction, pulp/paper and iron/steel were at the top of the list of advancing sectors.
The major decliners were communications, credit/lease and mining.

Although the Nikkei average is starting to show signs of improvement, some brokers said that the latest round of buying may not have enough momentum to lift the barometer past the next technical target.

"It has pushed past the 25- and 75-day moving averages but to test the 100-day average, which is above 18,800, a resumption of buying in high-technology shares may be needed," said Kunihiro Hatae, Tokyo Securities general manager.
Brokers added that the market was waiting to see how currencies react after the Group of Seven meeting on Saturday before considering buying blue-chip shares again.
In the domestic arena, brokers said the focus was on a two-day central bank branch managers' meeting which began today and official comments on the economy after a sales tax rise.

The broader TOPIX index added 18.04 points or 1.30 percent to end at 1,404.70. The Nikkei 300 rose 3.44 points or 1.28 percent to finish at 272.12. The second section index leaped 36.74 points or 2.34 percent to 1,609.27. Turnover was 10.68 million shares, up from 9.34 million in the previous session.
The over-the-counter index continued to rebound, rising 22.32 points or 2.03 percent to 1,120.90 in late Tokyo trade.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
